systems.name: WordPress
systems.support: Open-source project maintained by the WordPress contributor community; widely supported by hosting companies.
systems.technology: PHP server-side application; MySQL or MariaDB database; commonly Apache or Nginx; HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in the browser.
capabilities: Themes and a large plugin directory
Posts, pages, media library, users, and menus
REST API for integrations and headless websites
limitations: Self-hosted sites require maintenance of hosting, backups, updates, and security
Poorly maintained plugins or themes can cause vulnerabilities or conflicts
Complex customizations may require developer support

systems.name: Drupal
systems.support: Open-source project developed by the Drupal community, with documentation and community support through Drupal.org.
systems.technology: PHP; MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, or SQLite; Apache/Nginx and other compatible web servers; HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Flexible content types, fields, and taxonomies
Roles and permissions for complex editorial teams
limitations: Setup and configuration can be more complex than hosted builders
Advanced implementations often need experienced developers
Modules and custom code need compatibility checks during upgrades

systems.name: Joomla
systems.support: Open-source CMS maintained by the Joomla project and volunteer community; third-party hosting and professional support are available.
systems.technology: PHP; MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL; Apache, Nginx, or Microsoft IIS; HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Extensions provide components, modules, and plugins
limitations: Self-hosted installations require updates, backups, and security management
Some extensions cost extra or may not be maintained for newer releases

systems.name: Wix
systems.support: Commercial hosted website platform operated by Wix; hosting and platform maintenance are included with subscription plans.
systems.technology: Proprietary cloud platform. Wix manages server and database infrastructure. Browser output uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; CMS collections and APIs provide structured content; Velo supports custom development.
capabilities: APIs and Velo for custom functionality
limitations: Less control over server infrastructure than self-hosted CMS products
CMS quotas and data limits can depend on the plan
Moving the complete design and functionality to another platform may require rebuilding
Custom development is limited to supported tools and APIs

systems.name: Shopify
systems.support: Commercial hosted ecommerce platform operated by Shopify Inc.; subscription plans include hosted store services.
systems.technology: Proprietary hosted SaaS. Storefront themes use Liquid with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Shopify manages commerce backend, checkout, data storage, and hosting; APIs and apps extend functionality.
capabilities: Product catalog, inventory, cart, checkout, and orders
Themes and theme editor customize storefronts
App marketplace adds shipping, marketing, and reporting tools
APIs support integrations and custom storefronts
limitations: Subscription, payment, transaction, and app costs can add up
Advanced checkout and platform customization depend on plan and extension points
Less control over server and database than self-hosted software
Complex features may require paid apps or developer assistance
